title: Labcorp Launches Hepatitis D Reflex Testing to Enable Earlier Detection of the Most Severe Form of Viral Hepatitis
summary: Labcorp (NYSE: LH), a global leader of innovative and comprehensive laboratory services, today announced the availability of a new hepatitis D reflex testing option within its Comprehensive Hepatitis Testing portfolio.
body_markdown:
- Hepatitis D occurs only in people with hepatitis B and is associated with a higher risk of cirrhosis, liver cancer and other serious liver complications
- When ordered by a clinician, reflex testing automatically performs hepatitis D testing for patients who test positive for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)
- Supports earlier diagnosis as emerging hepatitis D treatment options increase the importance of timely detection


**BURLINGTON, N.C. (Aug. 25, 2026)** —[Labcorp](http://www.labcorp.com/) (NYSE: LH), a global leader of innovative and comprehensive laboratory services, today announced the availability of a new hepatitis D reflex testing option within its[Comprehensive Hepatitis Testing](https://www.labcorp.com/treatment-areas/virology-infectious-diseases/clinical-testing/hepatitis) portfolio. Because hepatitis D occurs only in people with hepatitis B, clinicians can now select a reflex testing option that automatically performs hepatitis D testing on the original blood sample when HBsAg is detected. This streamlined approach supports earlier diagnosis as emerging hepatitis D treatment options continue to advance.


**Addressing Gaps in Hepatitis D Detection**
An estimated[70,000 to 150,000](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10882855/) people in the United States are living with active hepatitis D infection, yet fewer than[20%](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10882855/) of hepatitis B-positive patients are tested for the disease. This gap in testing contributes to substantial underdiagnosis and delays in care.


With Labcorp's new reflex testing option, clinicians can elect automatic hepatitis D testing on the original blood sample for patients who test positive for HBsAg. This approach eliminates the need for a separate order and additional blood draws, helping clinicians obtain actionable results more quickly. Labcorp also offers enhanced hepatitis B reporting with simplified result interpretations designed to support clinical decision-making.


“Hepatitis D remains significantly underdiagnosed despite the serious consequences it can have for patients and long-term liver health,” said Brian Caveney, M.D., chief medical and scientific officer at Labcorp. “As treatment options continue to advance, identifying patients earlier is more important than ever. By integrating hepatitis D testing into the diagnostic workflow, we can help clinicians uncover infections that might otherwise go undetected and connect more patients to appropriate care sooner.” ****


**Building on a Proven Reflex Testing Model**
Labcorp's hepatitis D reflex testing builds on the company's experience using automated testing pathways to reduce diagnostic delays and improve follow-up care. Similar approaches have demonstrated value in[hepatitis C](https://academic.oup.com/cid/article-abstract/82/6/988/8643933?login=false) , where streamlined workflows have been associated with higher rates of confirmatory testing and faster diagnosis of active infection.


To learn more about Labcorp’s hepatitis testing portfolio, visit[https://www.labcorp.com/treatment-areas/virology-infectious-diseases/clinical-testing/hepatitis](https://www.labcorp.com/treatment-areas/virology-infectious-diseases/clinical-testing/hepatitis) .
